content:
Rumors suggest Apple's fall iPhone lineup this year will revolve around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Here are the three most significant feature differences—excluding price—that could influence your upgrade decision.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but worth mentioning because it's also the most important.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the basic iPhone form factor that's been used for years. The screen sizes and overall design of the two phones are rumored to be identical to their predecessors. If you want the feel of a traditional iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

The iPhone Ultra will be Apple's first foldable model. Its design is completely different, with an outer screen that's shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, and an inner screen similar to an iPad mini.

Cameras: Pro Still Reigns Supreme

Apple has always reserved its most cutting-edge and innovative camera technology for the Pro models. This year is no exception.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature largely the same camera capabilities as the iPhone 18 Pro, but with one major exception: it won't have a telephoto lens.

Rumors suggest the iPhone Ultra will share the same main lens, ultrawide lens, and front-facing camera as the Pro series. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro lineup, with specs rumored to be further upgraded this year.

Performance: Both Powered by A20 Pro Chip, but Materials Affect Real-World Performance

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to run on the A20 Pro chip at their core. However, due to differences in design and materials, performance levels between the two may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will retain the same all-aluminum unibody design used in the iPhone 17 Pro, and will also feature a vapor chamber cooling system. These two changes resulted in better overall performance for the iPhone 17 Pro compared to its predecessor, as the iPhone can maintain lower temperatures when handling demanding tasks.

The iPhone Ultra will adopt a sleek titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. While it may also include a vapor chamber, only one tipster has indicated this so far. However, due to the different materials, even with the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Ultra's performance may still lag slightly in direct sunlight or during intensive tasks.
